entry.title: Genesis Passing
entry.content:
2020-03-16

Back in 2017 I was able to see one of her last Psychic TV shows. Compared to say the Rolling Stones it was a small venue but the music was amazing and the light show and video.

Now she’s gone, cancer taken her in the end.

Ultimately all of us have a beginnging and end to a particular incarnation.

We don’t know how many will fall to this pandemic for example.

Now we don’t even know what will happen to music going forward.

Bands and artists made their living off lives shows.

When they get too sick like Genesis did they no longer have that income coming in and often have to live off the largess of fans.

Its sad that all people whether they’re senators or artists have access to healthcare.

But at the same time we all have a start and end to our incarnations barring the Singularity and some kind of brain dump into a machine.

But could such a “Singularity” be a fate worse than death?

Its hard to begin to describe the cultural impact of this artist and writer.

Her Topy Bible is a good starting point.

She also has an artist page on Spotify.

So it Begins.

At the same time that the vast majority of Americans in large cities are being severely thrown under a bus both parties are still spending trillions on the so called “defense industry.”

When you allow almost 200,000 people to die in a short amount of time due to sheer complacency what is the point of continuing to spend all the available resources on police and soldiers who ultimately kill our own people.

entry.title: Goodbye Dad
entry.content:
My father was born in 1941, right at the start of world world 2. He passed on 3/21/2020 at 645pm.

He was able to meet Charlie Mingus as the president of his university jazz club only to see the whole band get food poisoned by Johns Hopkins staff at the time.

Was it intentional food poisoning? Most likely Mingus would have thought it was, his music wasn’t exactly popular anywhere south of NYC.

My dad was in that tiny generation in between ww2 vets and the boomers. He was drafted before we got into Vietnam and served out his time in Germany rather than Indochina. He was a court reporter for the army at that time.

My favorite time, when we had a major power outage and he couldn’t go to work, extra time to bring out the old dungeons and dragons, my dad was an amazing dungeon master.

He worked his whole adult life for the army corps of engineers. He got a master’s in public policy and even though he was a life long republican became a big fan of Obama until he was unable to be a fan of anything besides the tv shows shown over and over on the tv at the home. He believed in data driven government, analytics and using science rather than violence to solve problems.

He’s not dying from the virus, he developed dementia around 10 years ago. Which is becoming more common especially in polluted southern california. Its a long slow death now he is finally coming to an end to being imprisoned in a broken body and his spirit can find freedom and the ecstacy of the union with OM. But we will miss him badly we have been missing him the whole time as he went into decline.

He always loved music, had one of the best vinyl collections outside of say somebody like Richard Branson who was rich and in the industry. Sadly his collection degraded from lack of play after he got his career going.

entry.title: The Song of Birds
entry.content:
Staying in place is easy for a writer, its our natural inclination not to go out.

Its a strange world where suddenly Howard Hughs is a major role model but its a real thing.

But more about that in a music review.

For now we sit here waiting to hear of my dad’s passing, my mom completely torutured but what can one do?

We never know how long we have here, my friend lost his son and nephew to a car accident they were only 14. In many ways we make this place a lot more dangerous than it has to be in order for a few to benefit.

Here we can hardly stand a medical emergency yet the powers that be still seek war and confrontation. When can we have peace and cooperation with a focus on happiness, kindness and compassion?

Now I just focus on two things, what can I do to help and what can I learn while I have a lot of time to sit and read.

Try to clear my mind and make every action a meditation. While I’m completely freaked out of course but its important to acknowledge the fear give it its due but then put it away.

This is a great time to study online we have many great resources, I always like to point out khan academy because they’re free and open to anyone.

entry.title: A Story
entry.content:
On the Beach, Why am I here? To get a tan? To praise the sun or the scratchy sand that beneath buttocks, or to praise the waves?

Or write ocean-polluted poetry of overburden? Ridden by copper-tanned straddling saddles Of fiberglass.

The sand is strewn with celluloid debris sacrificing write-ups to the sunless sky, wall to wall people, waves of flesh against waves of water, American music from transistor radios, and all the sand, sky and celluloid are one.

Life could be a Sci-Fi novel. Ads praising toilet paper like the messiah,

Phallic ships soaring to the moon, or to deliver atomic death, couch potatoes collect radiation from their TV sets,

While models collect cash for their printed photons. They glorify themselvesn their stinkin' tobacco and cheap cheapo.

Heat is the sponge that soaks up hope. It burns, heats and melts, dragging away life, sucking like an infant's mouth upon the nipple of life.

When do you kill? you fill the drainage ditch with bodies, to satisfy you lust, cravings of your mad gods.

Do the gods listen, or do they simply float away, on a cloud or non-existence.

You make the world stink with the stench of burning flesh body.

But only the youth, children die.

They say that your gods are the worst.

But I think not. You sacrifice fourteen, but ten million die for the Power.

entry.title: I Understand
entry.content:
I understand it, The junkey is the most profound expression of desperation.

They tell him to leave it, so he seceeds from America, into his own country, the country of his own mind.

Hippies tried to change things, and when they couldn't change it, many of them became junkeys, alcoholics, seceeded from this country, into their own.

This doesn't mean that this is right, and its definitely self-destructive, but that's what happened.

Jimi Hendrix and Dylan were great, because they were able to transcend the inherent limitations of the genres that they chose to work through.

Jimi started out playing the blues, but he had so much more to say, that he expanded and shattered it to reveal a whole new territory.

Dylan did the same with white folk, He started out imitating Woody Guthrie, but when he came against the wall, he burst through it, because he had too much to say.

They both embraced new technology.

I was very angry today, I was frustrated with everything, and I felt like I wanted to kill everything.
